name: Rod Y
description: Approximates a rigid rod of fixed length as a stiff spring and damper along its axis, a standard way to hold two bodies a set distance apart without a constraint solver. This is the Y component, to use alongside Rod X between the same two bodies; a Z version has to be added by hand for out-of-plane motion, since an edge acts on one state. Connect it between two Free bodies (source and target); it reads both bodies' positions and the Y velocities, and acts on the target's Y velocity. Rest length (m, default 1) is the length the rod wants to be. Stiffness (N/m, default 500) is how hard it pushes back for each metre it is stretched or squashed; larger holds the length more tightly. Damping (N·s/m, default 10) resists the two bodies moving relative to each other, and settles oscillation. Mass (kg, default 0.5) is the mass of the target body, used to turn the force into an acceleration; set it to match the body. The damping is applied separately on each axis instead of strictly along the rod, a small simplification that changes how quickly the rod settles, not where it ends up. For a body that nothing else drives (a passive joint) this alone holds it at a fixed distance from the other end.
